File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Webworm: New burrowing techniques
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] EchoCreep Discord API beacon from non-browser process (Webworm 2025) · [LLM] GraphWorm OneDrive /createUploadSession C2 from non-Office process · [LLM] Webworm 2025 IOC match — known C2 IPs (Vultr/IT7) and file hashes · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] WormFrp / Webworm Amazon S3 staging bucket access (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
EchoCreep Discord API beacon from non-browser process (Webworm 2025) AICommand & Control High
Hunts the EchoCreep backdoor's Discord-based C2 channel: a script interpreter or non-browser process beaconing to discord.com / discordapp.com API endpoints to upload files, fetch jobs, and run cmd.exe shell commands. ESET decrypted 400+ Discord messages and four guild/channel pairs tied to this campaign. Rationale: Article anchors EchoCreep to Discord API calls for upload/download/shell/sleep (Table 1) and explicitly states the backdoor's network traffic 'passes through Discord APIs using crafted HTTP requests'. Excluding the genuine Discord client + browsers leaves only the C2 path. Cross-checked Mandiant's Discord-C2 pattern guidance to confirm exclusion list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://www.symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/webworm-espionage-rats
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod or curl.exe against Discord webhooks for legitimate notifications
  • Game launchers (non-Discord) embedding Discord rich-presence calls via custom binaries
  • Custom helpdesk bots calling Discord API from a scheduled task using powershell.exe
  • Security tools that fetch indicator feeds from Discord-hosted gists
  • First-party Discord beta builds with non-standard EXE names
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","powershell.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("webhooks/","@everyone","slash-command") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("devops","build-bot"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and parent chain; if it's a script interpreter spawned by Office, browser, or unknown parent, escalate. Validate the user's intent (do they own a Discord bot script?). 2) Contain — isolate the host via Defender LiveResponse, kill the InitiatingProcessId, and block the destination Discord channel ID at the proxy if extractable from packet capture. 3) Hunt — search 30 days for the same parent-process hash across the estate, pivot on InitiatingProcessFolderPath for staged binaries, and query DeviceFileEvents for any GitHub-staged droppers (SoftEther, iox, frp) on the same host.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Discord.exe","DiscordPTB.exe","DiscordCanary.exe","Spotify.exe","slack.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WebexTeams.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, NewProcessId;
let DiscordTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
       or Url has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/","discord.com/api","discordapp.com/api")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
DiscordTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstNet desc
title: EchoCreep Discord C2 from Non-Browser Process

description: Detects EchoCreep (Webworm APT, 2025) backdoor C2 traffic to Discord APIs initiated by a script interpreter or non-browser binary.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1102.002
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_dst:
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - 'discord.com'
      - 'discordapp.com'
      - 'discord.gg'
      - 'cdn.discordapp.com'
  filter_legit_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\Discord.exe'
      - '\DiscordPTB.exe'
      - '\DiscordCanary.exe'
      - '\slack.exe'
      - '\Teams.exe'
      - '\Spotify.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
      - '\opera.exe'
  condition: selection_dst and not filter_legit_image
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*discord.com OR *discordapp.com OR *discord.gg OR *cdn.discordapp.com) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\MsEdge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\Discord.exe OR *\\DiscordPTB.exe OR *\\DiscordCanary.exe OR *\\slack.exe OR *\\Slack.exe OR *\\Teams.exe OR *\\Spotify.exe OR *\\iexplore.exe OR *\\opera.exe)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest (DomainName=/discord(app)?\.com$/i OR DomainName=/discord\.gg$/i OR DomainName=/cdn\.discordapp\.com$/i)
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|cscript|wscript|rundll32|regsvr32|mshta|curl|wget)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| _count >= 3
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com") OR All_Traffic.url IN ("*discord.com/api/v9/*","*discord.com/api/v10/*","*discordapp.com/api/*")) by All_Traffic.src,All_Traffic.dest,All_Traffic.user,All_Traffic.process_name,All_Traffic.url,_time | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | search NOT (process_name IN ("*\\chrome.exe","*\\msedge.exe","*\\firefox.exe","*\\brave.exe","*\\opera.exe","*\\iexplore.exe","*\\Discord.exe","*\\DiscordPTB.exe","*\\DiscordCanary.exe","*\\Spotify.exe","*\\slack.exe","*\\Teams.exe")) | stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen sum(count) as conn_count values(url) as urls dc(_time) as connection_buckets by src,user,process_name,dest | where conn_count>=3
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com") OR All_Traffic.url IN ("*discord.com/api/v9/*","*discord.com/api/v10/*","*discordapp.com/api/*")) by All_Traffic.src,All_Traffic.dest,All_Traffic.user,All_Traffic.process_name,All_Traffic.url,_time | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | search NOT (process_name IN ("*\\chrome.exe","*\\msedge.exe","*\\firefox.exe","*\\brave.exe","*\\opera.exe","*\\iexplore.exe","*\\Discord.exe","*\\DiscordPTB.exe","*\\DiscordCanary.exe","*\\Spotify.exe","*\\slack.exe","*\\Teams.exe")) | stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen sum(count) as conn_count values(url) as urls dc(_time) as connection_buckets by src,user,process_name,dest | where conn_count>=3
GraphWorm OneDrive /createUploadSession C2 from non-Office process AICommand & Control High
Hunts GraphWorm backdoor C2: Microsoft Graph API calls to /createUploadSession and victim-specific OneDrive directories from a non-Office, non-Edge process. ESET observed GraphWorm exclusively using OneDrive endpoints to fetch jobs and upload large staged files, with a separate directory per victim. Rationale: Article explicitly names the abused endpoint: 'the Microsoft Graph API endpoint /createUploadSession to upload large, staged files' and confines GraphWorm to OneDrive paths per-victim. Excluding native Office/OneDrive/Edge processes preserves the malicious signal while suppressing legit Graph use. Cross-referenced MITRE ATT&CK T1102.002 and Microsoft's Graph API consumer list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/driveitem-createuploadsession
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PowerShell scripts using Microsoft Graph SDK for legitimate SharePoint/OneDrive automation
  • Backup or DLP agents using custom EXEs to enumerate user OneDrive content via Graph
  • Developer testing of /createUploadSession via Postman renamed to a custom binary
  • Power Automate Desktop using a bespoke runtime that hits Graph endpoints
  • Identity governance tools doing user-drive inventory via Graph
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pwsh.exe","powershell.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Microsoft.Graph","Connect-MgGraph","Invoke-MgGraphRequest") and InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("itadmin","sharepoint-svc"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — review InitiatingProcessCommandLine and parent for legitimate dev/admin context; check if the user has Graph SDK installed or scheduled tasks calling Graph. 2) Contain — isolate device, kill the offending process tree, revoke OAuth tokens scoped to Files.ReadWrite for that user via AAD audit. 3) Hunt — enumerate AADSignInEventsBeta for the same user's Graph token issuance, search for victim-specific OneDrive directories created via Office365 OneDrive audit logs, and pivot on InitiatingProcessSHA256 to find GraphWorm sibling implants estate-wide.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.microsoft.com"
   and (RemoteUrl has "createUploadSession" or RemoteUrl has "/me/drive/items" or RemoteUrl has "/drives/" or RemoteUrl has "/me/drive/root:")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","OneDrive.exe","OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WINWORD.EXE","EXCEL.EXE","POWERPNT.EXE","OUTLOOK.EXE","ONENOTE.EXE","Outlook.exe","officeclicktorun.exe","backgroundtaskhost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\curl.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine;
let GraphTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has "graph.microsoft.com"
       and (Url has "createUploadSession" or Url has "/me/drive/items" or Url has "/drives/" or Url has "/me/drive/root:")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
GraphTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| order by FirstNet desc

WormFrp / Webworm Amazon S3 staging bucket access (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts contact with the compromised Amazon S3 buckets Webworm uses to stage configs, VM snapshots, mRemoteNG XMLs and SharpSecretsdump. Article names two buckets — wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com and whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com — used both for retrieving WormFrp configurations and exfiltrating data from victims in Italy and Spain. Rationale: Article cites exact bucket FQDNs (wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com and whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com). Any host in our estate touching these substrings is high-fidelity Webworm contact — the buckets are publicly documented IOCs taken down by ESET. No baseline exclusions needed. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform fetching IOC samples from the same buckets after takedown (post-takedown re-resolution attempts)
  • SIEM enrichment lookup hitting the bucket name as DNS query when validating ingested IOCs
  • Security researcher revisiting the bucket from a corporate sandbox
  • DNS sinkhole appliance generating echo responses for blocked IOC FQDNs
  • VirusTotal Retro-Hunt notification webhook including the URL in payload
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("misp-modules.exe","opencti.exe","yara.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("misp","opencti","threatfox","virustotal-retrohunt"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the initiating process, account, and full URL path; if response code is 200 and bytes >0, treat as confirmed retrieval. Determine whether host downloaded WormFrp config or uploaded VM snapshots/credentials. 2) Contain — isolate host, kill the requesting process, block both bucket FQDNs at proxy/DNS, and rotate any credentials touched on that host (especially mRemoteNG saved profiles). 3) Hunt — search DeviceFileEvents for SharpSecretsdump, iox, frp, SoftEther, mRemoteNG XML exports written in the last 30 days; pivot DeviceNetworkEvents to the known Vultr/IT7 C2 IPs (45.77.13.67, 64.176.85.158, 104.243.23.43, 108.61.200.151, 144.168.60.233) from the same host.
let WebwormBuckets = dynamic(["wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com","whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com","wamanharipethe.s3.amazonaws.com"]);
let WebwormBucketSubstrings = dynamic(["wamanharipethe","whpjewellers"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| union (
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType has "Dns"
| where AdditionalFields has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings) or RemoteUrl has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl=coalesce(RemoteUrl,tostring(AdditionalFields)), RemoteIP, RemotePort=toint(0), ActionType
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebwormBucketSubstrings = dynamic(["wamanharipethe","whpjewellers"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="DNS", Host=Computer, SrcIp=ClientIP, Destination=Name, Detail=tostring(QueryType)
),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationHostName has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or RequestURL has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct), Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, Destination=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Detail=RequestURL
),
(ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstHostname has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or Url has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Destination=DstHostname, Detail=Url
),
(ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where HttpHostName has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or Url has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Destination=HttpHostName, Detail=Url
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Webworm Compromised S3 Bucket Access (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers)
id: 1c3e7d9a-bc12-4d2f-90ff-7b8a3c0d11d2
description: Detects host contact with the two Amazon S3 buckets used by Webworm (WormFrp) in the 2025 campaign for tool staging and victim data exfiltration.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.t1567.002
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: dns
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'wamanharipethe'
      - 'whpjewellers'
  condition: selection
level: high
(@DestinationHostname:(*wamanharipethe* OR *whpjewellers*) OR @DomainName:(*wamanharipethe* OR *whpjewellers*) OR @http.url:(*wamanharipethe* OR *whpjewellers*) OR @network.destination.domain:(*wamanharipethe* OR *whpjewellers*))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest AND DomainName=/wamanharipethe|whpjewellers/i)
OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 AND ContextImageFileName=/.*/)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())

Webworm 2025 IOC match — known C2 IPs (Vultr/IT7) and file hashes AICommand & Control Medium
Atomic IOC match for the five Webworm C2 IPs (Vultr / IT7 Networks) and the six SHA1 hashes published by ESET for WormFrp, ChainWorm, SmuxProxy, WormSocket, EchoCreep, and GraphWorm samples observed in 2025. Rationale: Direct atomic IOC match on values published in the ESET article: five Vultr/IT7 C2 IPs and six SHA1 hashes. The article ties the Vultr/IT7 IP block to confirmed Webworm proxy/VPN infrastructure (article: 'All Webworm proxies and VPN services are cloud servers that belong to network infrastructure controlled by Vultr and IT7 Networks'). Zero baseline contact expected in a benign estate. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/webworm-espionage-rats
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.001 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform downloading the same SHA1 indicators from VT/MISP and writing them to local disk for enrichment
  • Researcher analyst sandbox detonating the published sample for verification
  • Red-team purple exercise replaying Webworm samples for SOC tuning
  • DNS sinkhole/IDS reflecting decoy traffic back into the same telemetry pipeline
  • Legitimate Vultr-hosted SaaS that incidentally shares an IP with one of the five (verify CIDR before suppression)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("misp.exe","opencti.exe","yara.exe","virustotal.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("download_sample","vt-cli","misp-modules"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — confirm the IOC was hit by a production endpoint (not researcher/sandbox tag) and capture full process / file / network context; pull PCAP if available. 2) Contain — isolate host(s) via EDR, kill matching processes, quarantine matching binaries on disk, block all five IPs at perimeter, and add the hashes to AV/EDR custom-IOC list. 3) Hunt — sweep last 90 days estate-wide for any of the six hashes, the two S3 buckets (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers), Discord API / Graph /createUploadSession beaconing patterns, and SoftEther/iox/frp binaries on disk; review GitHub repo `github.com/anjsdgasdf/WordPress` artifact downloads.
let WebwormIPs = dynamic(["45.77.13.67","64.176.85.158","104.243.23.43","108.61.200.151","144.168.60.233"]);
let WebwormHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98","1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7","7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB","77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217","948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6","A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (WebwormIPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="IP", Indicator=RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="SHA1", Indicator=SHA1, RemotePort=toint(0), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath=FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in (WebwormHashes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="SHA1", Indicator=coalesce(SHA1,InitiatingProcessSHA1), RemotePort=toint(0), InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath=FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebwormIPs = dynamic(["45.77.13.67","64.176.85.158","104.243.23.43","108.61.200.151","144.168.60.233"]);
let WebwormHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98","1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7","7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB","77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217","948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6","A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP in (WebwormIPs) or SourceIP in (WebwormIPs) or FileHash in (WebwormHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct), Host=SourceHostName, IndicatorType=iff(DestinationIP in (WebwormIPs) or SourceIP in (WebwormIPs),"IP","Hash"), Indicator=iff(DestinationIP in (WebwormIPs),DestinationIP, iff(SourceIP in (WebwormIPs),SourceIP,FileHash)), Detail=strcat("port=",tostring(DestinationPort))
),
(ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (WebwormIPs) or SrcIpAddr in (WebwormIPs)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, IndicatorType="IP", Indicator=iff(DstIpAddr in (WebwormIPs),DstIpAddr,SrcIpAddr), Detail=strcat("port=",tostring(DstPortNumber))
),
(ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA1 in (WebwormHashes) or Hash in (WebwormHashes) or TargetFileSHA256 in (WebwormHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, IndicatorType="Hash", Indicator=coalesce(TargetFileSHA1,TargetFileSHA256,Hash), Detail=TargetFilePath
),
(ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes) or Hash in (WebwormHashes) or SHA256 in (WebwormHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, IndicatorType="Hash", Indicator=coalesce(SHA1,SHA256,Hash), Detail=ActingProcessCommandLine
)

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2017-7692")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2017-7692")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"

          ParentProcessName

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or SHA1 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or MD5 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or SHA1 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or MD5 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e3798c71d25816611a4cab031ae3c27a", "0f9c5408335833e72fe73e6166b5a01b", "cd36a3071a315c3be6ac3366d80bb59c", "9f880ac607cbd7cdfffa609c5883c708", "6a89fbe7b0d526e3d97b0da8418bf851", "3a33013a47c5dd8d1b92a4cfdcda3765", "7a62295f70642fedf0d5a5637feb7986", "467eef090deb3517f05a48310fcfd4ee", "4a47404fc21fff4a1bc492f9cd23139c") or SHA1 in~ ("e3798c71d25816611a4cab031ae3c27a", "0f9c5408335833e72fe73e6166b5a01b", "cd36a3071a315c3be6ac3366d80bb59c", "9f880ac607cbd7cdfffa609c5883c708", "6a89fbe7b0d526e3d97b0da8418bf851", "3a33013a47c5dd8d1b92a4cfdcda3765", "7a62295f70642fedf0d5a5637feb7986", "467eef090deb3517f05a48310fcfd4ee", "4a47404fc21fff4a1bc492f9cd23139c") or MD5 in~ ("e3798c71d25816611a4cab031ae3c27a", "0f9c5408335833e72fe73e6166b5a01b", "cd36a3071a315c3be6ac3366d80bb59c", "9f880ac607cbd7cdfffa609c5883c708", "6a89fbe7b0d526e3d97b0da8418bf851", "3a33013a47c5dd8d1b92a4cfdcda3765", "7a62295f70642fedf0d5a5637feb7986", "467eef090deb3517f05a48310fcfd4ee", "4a47404fc21fff4a1bc492f9cd23139c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e3798c71d25816611a4cab031ae3c27a", "0f9c5408335833e72fe73e6166b5a01b", "cd36a3071a315c3be6ac3366d80bb59c", "9f880ac607cbd7cdfffa609c5883c708", "6a89fbe7b0d526e3d97b0da8418bf851", "3a33013a47c5dd8d1b92a4cfdcda3765", "7a62295f70642fedf0d5a5637feb7986", "467eef090deb3517f05a48310fcfd4ee", "4a47404fc21fff4a1bc492f9cd23139c") or SHA1 in~ ("e3798c71d25816611a4cab031ae3c27a", "0f9c5408335833e72fe73e6166b5a01b", "cd36a3071a315c3be6ac3366d80bb59c", "9f880ac607cbd7cdfffa609c5883c708", "6a89fbe7b0d526e3d97b0da8418bf851", "3a33013a47c5dd8d1b92a4cfdcda3765", "7a62295f70642fedf0d5a5637feb7986", "467eef090deb3517f05a48310fcfd4ee", "4a47404fc21fff4a1bc492f9cd23139c") or MD5 in~ ("e3798c71d25816611a4cab031ae3c27a", "0f9c5408335833e72fe73e6166b5a01b", "cd36a3071a315c3be6ac3366d80bb59c", "9f880ac607cbd7cdfffa609c5883c708", "6a89fbe7b0d526e3d97b0da8418bf851", "3a33013a47c5dd8d1b92a4cfdcda3765", "7a62295f70642fedf0d5a5637feb7986", "467eef090deb3517f05a48310fcfd4ee", "4a47404fc21fff4a1bc492f9cd23139c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["e3798c71d25816611a4cab031ae3c27a", "0f9c5408335833e72fe73e6166b5a01b", "cd36a3071a315c3be6ac3366d80bb59c", "9f880ac607cbd7cdfffa609c5883c708", "6a89fbe7b0d526e3d97b0da8418bf851", "3a33013a47c5dd8d1b92a4cfdcda3765", "7a62295f70642fedf0d5a5637feb7986", "467eef090deb3517f05a48310fcfd4ee", "4a47404fc21fff4a1bc492f9cd23139c"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

CISA KEV: CVE-2010-0806 — Microsoft Internet Explorer Use-After-Free Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-05-20 1 use case 0 techniques 2 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft Internet Explorer contains an use-after-free vulnerability that could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via vectors involving access to an invalid pointer after the deletion of an object. The impacted product could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users should discontinue product utilization. Vendor: Microsoft, Product: Internet Explorer. Federal patch due: 2026-06-03.

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AWS SSM SendCommand Fan-out from EC2 Instance Role (TeamPCP Worm Propagation) · [LLM] Python Process Reading Multi-Cloud Credential Stores (durabletask Stealer Stage) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI Package Install (TeamPCP 1.4.1-1.4.3) AIDelivery High
Detects pip/python installing the TeamPCP-compromised durabletask versions (1.4.0-1.4.3) — Microsoft's Durable Task Python SDK was published with a malicious dropper that fetches rope.pyz. Article-specific because it pins the exact package + version range named in the campaign. Rationale: Anchors on the exact package name 'durabletask' and version range from the article's code blocks plus external corroboration (Wiz, safedep, Aikido confirmed 1.4.1-1.4.3 as the malicious versions published 2026-05-19). pip+package-name+specific-version is high-fidelity — there is no legitimate reason to pin those exact malicious versions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/microsofts-durabletask-pypi-package-compromised-in-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security/IR team intentionally installing a malicious version in an isolated sandbox for reverse engineering
  • Threat-intel feed ingestion pipeline that downloads PyPI tarballs for scanning (Snyk, Socket, OSV-Scanner workers)
  • Developer running `pip install durabletask==1.4.x` against a private PyPI mirror that still has cached malicious artifacts after the official yank
  • Backup/restore of an older requirements.txt that pinned the malicious version
  • CI re-running an old build manifest that still references the malicious version
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dry-run","--download","--no-deps") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "-d ") and not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","malware-lab","snyk-scanner","socket-scanner"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Confirm version installed via `pip show durabletask` on host; cross-check requirements.txt / poetry.lock / pipfile.lock against 1.4.1-1.4.3. Identify host context (developer laptop, CI runner, prod build agent). Step 2 (Contain): Isolate host from network. Force-uninstall the package and inspect ~/.cache/, /tmp/, and ~/.local/lib/python*/site-packages/durabletask for dropped artifacts. Rotate any AWS/GCP/Azure/GitHub/npm credentials accessible from that host or its IAM role. Step 3 (Hunt): Pivot to UC2 (rope.pyz network fetch) and UC3 (infection marker files) on the same host. Query CI/CD logs for any builds that pulled 1.4.1-1.4.3 and treat downstream artifacts as suspect.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Installation of Compromised durabletask PyPI Versions (TeamPCP)
id: a1f47e8c-9b3d-4d2c-9e1a-7b5c4f8e9d2a
description: Detects pip/python installing durabletask versions 1.4.1-1.4.3, the TeamPCP-compromised supply-chain releases of Microsoft's Durable Task Python SDK that drop rope.pyz.

author: SOC Detection Engineering

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*/pip OR */pip3 OR */python OR */python3 OR */python3.10 OR */python3.11 OR */python3.12) @process.command_line:(*durabletask*1.4.1* OR *durabletask*1.4.2* OR *durabletask*1.4.3* OR *durabletask==1.4.*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(pip|pip3|python|python3(\.\d+)?)$/i CommandLine=/durabletask.*(1\.4\.[0-3]|==1\.4\.)/i

| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("pip","pip3","python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") AND (Processes.process="*durabletask*1.4.1*" OR Processes.process="*durabletask*1.4.2*" OR Processes.process="*durabletask*1.4.3*" OR Processes.process="*durabletask==1.4.*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | sort 0 -_time
TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Fetch from check.git-service.com C2 AICommand & Control Medium
Detects DNS, HTTP, or direct-IP egress to the TeamPCP C2 infrastructure that hosts the durabletask second-stage dropper (rope.pyz). Article-specific because it pins the exact filename and the campaign's named C2 domains. Rationale: Uses the exact payload filename 'rope.pyz' from article code-block 3 and the campaign C2 domain check.git-service.com confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido. No legitimate developer infrastructure resolves these domains — they were registered 2026-05-16 by the actor and have no clean use case. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-investigating-teampcp-claimed.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security tooling resolving the C2 to confirm sinkhole status (Cisco Umbrella, Quad9 lookup)
  • Threat-intel platform proactively fetching the payload for analysis (VirusTotal, urlscan.io workers)
  • Analyst manually browsing the domain during incident triage
  • Honeypot or threat-research host intentionally beaconing to the C2
  • Pre-blocked DNS resolution where the egress is denied but the query is still logged
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("VirusTotal","urlscan","vt-scanner") and DeviceName has_any ("threat-intel","sandbox","sinkhole"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Identify the initiating process — if it's python/pip, treat as confirmed durabletask compromise. Capture full process tree and any files written under /tmp/ or ~/.cache/ in the surrounding 60s. Step 2 (Contain): Block check.git-service.com, t.m-kosche.com, and the IPs 160.119.64.3, 83.142.209.194 at egress and DNS. Isolate the host. Step 3 (Hunt): Pivot to UC3 (look for /tmp/rope-*.pyz, /tmp/managed.pyz, ~/.cache/.sys-update-check on the same host) and UC4 (any AWS SSM SendCommand calls from this host's IAM role in the last 24h). Rotate every credential reachable from the host.
union
( DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any ("check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com","rope.pyz")
      or RemoteIP in ("160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Process=InitiatingProcessFileName, Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Evt="NetworkConnect"
),
( DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | where AdditionalFields has_any ("check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com","git-service.com")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Process=InitiatingProcessFileName, Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP="", RemoteUrl=tostring(AdditionalFields), RemotePort=int(null), Evt="DnsQuery"
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
( ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any ("check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com","git-service.com")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Indicator=DnsQuery, Channel="DNS"
),
( ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Url has_any ("rope.pyz","check.git-service.com")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Indicator=Url, Channel="HTTP"
),
( ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DstIpAddr in ("160.119.64.3","83.142.209.194")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Indicator=DstIpAddr, Channel="NetworkConnect"
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Infection Markers on Linux AIInstallation High
Detects creation of TeamPCP's on-disk artifacts from the durabletask compromise: the rope.pyz / managed.pyz dropper payloads in /tmp/ and the ~/.cache/.sys-update-check infection marker. Article-specific because rope.pyz is named verbatim in code block 3. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim 'rope.pyz' filename from article code block 3, plus the marker files /tmp/managed.pyz and ~/.cache/.sys-update-check confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido as the dropper's on-disk artifacts. None of these paths/filenames have legitimate Linux usage — they are unique to this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR team copying the captured rope.pyz sample to /tmp/ on a forensics box for analysis
  • Security researcher unpacking the artifact in a sandbox VM
  • Malware-zoo / yara-rule build machine syncing samples
  • Backup restore of an already-infected host into a clean environment (file re-created during restore)
  • File-recovery tool replaying journal entries that include the dropper write
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("forensics","malware-lab","sandbox","yara-builder") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("ir-analyst","malware-research"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Compute SHA-256 of the dropped file and compare to the public IOC 069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce. Identify the writing process (almost always python/pip when caused by durabletask). Step 2 (Contain): Isolate host. Kill any live python process descended from the install. Delete the marker files only AFTER capturing forensic copies. Step 3 (Hunt): Search for AWS SSM SendCommand from this host's IAM role (UC4), kubectl exec from this host's kubeconfig context, and any Python access to ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gcloud/, ~/.kube/config in the surrounding hour (UC5).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has "/tmp/" and (FileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or FileName =~ "rope.pyz" or FileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (FolderPath has "/.cache/" and FileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath has "/tmp/" and (TargetFileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or TargetFileName =~ "rope.pyz" or TargetFileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.cache/" and TargetFileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Artifact on Linux (durabletask Supply Chain)
id: e3a7b1d4-9c2e-4f6a-b8d5-1e3c7a9b5d2f
description: Detects creation of TeamPCP infection markers used by the durabletask PyPI supply-chain compromise — /tmp/rope-*.pyz, /tmp/managed.pyz dropper files or the ~/.cache/.sys-update-check infection marker.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_dropper:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/tmp/rope-'
      - '/tmp/managed.pyz'
      - '/tmp/rope.pyz'
  selection_marker:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/.cache/.sys-update-check'
  condition: selection_dropper or selection_marker
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog OR windows.sysmon) (@file.path:(*/tmp/rope-*.pyz OR */tmp/rope.pyz OR */tmp/managed.pyz OR */.cache/.sys-update-check OR */.cache/.sys-update-check-k8s) OR @TargetFilename:(*\/tmp\/rope-*.pyz OR *\/tmp\/managed.pyz OR */.cache/.sys-update-check*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/(\/tmp\/rope(-[^\/]+)?\.pyz|\/tmp\/managed\.pyz|\/\.cache\/\.sys-update-check(-k8s)?$)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
| Hash:=SHA256HashData
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/rope-*.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/managed.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cache/.sys-update-check" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cache/.sys-update-check-k8s" OR Filesystem.file_name="rope.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_name="managed.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_name=".sys-update-check" OR Filesystem.file_name=".sys-update-check-k8s") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort 0 -_time
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/rope-*.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/managed.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cache/.sys-update-check" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cache/.sys-update-check-k8s" OR Filesystem.file_name="rope.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_name="managed.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_name=".sys-update-check" OR Filesystem.file_name=".sys-update-check-k8s") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort 0 -_time
AWS SSM SendCommand Fan-out from EC2 Instance Role (TeamPCP Worm Propagation) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask worm's lateral-movement stage: a single EC2-instance IAM role calling ssm:SendCommand against multiple EC2 instances within a short window. The rope.pyz worm uses stolen instance-role credentials to push itself to peer instances via SSM RunCommand. Rationale: Captures the worm's worm-stage primitive (ssm:SendCommand from an instance role to peer instances) which Wiz and safedep flagged as the AWS-specific propagation method. CloudTrail-only — Defender XDR and Falcon FDR don't ingest AWS control-plane events, hence empty defender_kql / falcon_logscale_query. Sentinel has the AWSCloudTrail connector but the table isn't in our canonical schema, so left empty rather than guess column names. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1651 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager performing batch patching across an instance fleet
  • AWS Config Conformance Pack remediation calling SendCommand for compliance fixes
  • SSM Automation document execution as part of a scheduled maintenance window
  • IaC tooling (Ansible AWX, Salt) using an SSM-based connection broker against a fleet
  • Operations runbook running an `aws ssm send-command` from a jump host across many instances
Suppression filter
| where source_role!="AWSServiceRoleForAmazonSSM*" AND source_role!="*PatchManager*" AND source_role!="*ConfigRecorder*" AND 'requestParameters.documentName'!="AWS-RunPatchBaseline" AND 'requestParameters.documentName'!="AWS-UpdateSSMAgent"
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Confirm the calling IAM role is an EC2 instance role (not a human user, not a service like Patch Manager). Look up the source EC2 instance via instance-profile-arn lookup. Check whether that source instance shows the rope.pyz markers (UC3). Step 2 (Contain): Revoke the instance-profile session credentials (call `aws iam delete-role-session` or terminate the instance). Pause the SSM document/association on the source role. Step 3 (Hunt): Pull the SendCommand `parameters.commands` payload — TeamPCP base64-embeds the curl-to-check.git-service.com fetcher. For each instance in `requestParameters.instanceIds`, run UC3 (infection-marker hunt) to confirm worm spread.
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:SendCommand @userIdentity.type:AssumedRole @requestParameters.instanceIds:* (-@userAgent:(*aws-cli/* AND *root/*) AND -@userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName:(*ssm-automation* OR *patch-manager* OR *config-rule*))
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` eventName=SendCommand eventSource="ssm.amazonaws.com" "userIdentity.type"="AssumedRole" 
| eval source_role=mvindex(split('userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn',"/"),-1)
| eval target_count=mvcount('requestParameters.instanceIds{}')
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen dc('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as DistinctTargets values('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as Targets values(sourceIPAddress) as SourceIPs values(userAgent) as UAs by source_role 'userIdentity.arn' awsRegion
| where DistinctTargets >= 3 OR like(source_role, "%ec2%") OR like(source_role, "%-instance-%")
| sort 0 -last_seen
Python Process Reading Multi-Cloud Credential Stores (durabletask Stealer Stage) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single Python process opening credential files from THREE OR MORE distinct cloud/dev ecosystems within a 5-minute window — the signature behaviour of the rope.pyz multi-cloud stealer that harvests AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, GitHub, Docker, and SSH secrets in one pass. Rationale: Targets the rope.pyz second-stage behaviour that Wiz and safedep documented: a single python process enumerating credentials across AWS + Azure + GCP + Kubernetes + npm + GitHub + Docker + SSH within seconds. The DistinctSecretFamilies>=3 threshold eliminates legitimate cloud SDKs that touch one ecosystem at a time while still catching the multi-cloud stealer in a single hit. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Multi-cloud Terraform/Pulumi runs that initialise AWS+Azure+GCP providers (python child of terraform/pulumi)
  • Cloud-cost-management tools like Infracost or CloudHealth agent that read all provider credentials
  • Backup tooling (Restic, Velero) that needs credentials for multi-cloud target buckets
  • Developer running `cloudquery sync` or `steampipe query` against multiple providers
  • An IaC validation script (Checkov, tfsec) being pointed at a multi-cloud config tree
Suppression filter
| where not (Cmd has_any ("terraform","pulumi","ansible","checkov","tfsec","infracost","cloudquery","steampipe","velero","restic")) and not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("terraform","pulumi","ansible-playbook"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Capture the python process tree and command line. If parent is pip/durabletask install context OR the process is short-lived (<60s wall time) with no TTY, treat as confirmed stealer. If parent is terraform/pulumi/ansible/checkov/restic, likely benign — verify the binary's parent. Step 2 (Contain): Kill the process. Rotate all credentials in each SecretFamily the process touched (AWS access keys, Azure SP secrets, GCP service-account keys, kubeconfig tokens, npm tokens, GitHub PATs). Step 3 (Hunt): Pivot to UC2 (look for any subsequent egress to check.git-service.com from the host) and UC4 (check AWS SSM SendCommand from any of the rotated AWS IAM principals during the exposure window). Audit GitHub PAT use across the org for anomalous repo-clone bursts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    FolderPath has "/.aws/","aws",
    FolderPath has "/.azure/","azure",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    FolderPath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    FolderPath has "/.docker/","docker",
    FileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    FileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gh/" and FileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    FolderPath has "/.ssh/" and FileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(strcat(FolderPath,"/",FileName), 20), Cmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(Timestamp, *) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    TargetFilePath has "/.aws/","aws",
    TargetFilePath has "/.azure/","azure",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    TargetFilePath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    TargetFilePath has "/.docker/","docker",
    TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    TargetFileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gh/" and TargetFileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    TargetFilePath has "/.ssh/" and TargetFileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20), Cmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessId, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| case {
    TargetFileName=/\.aws\// | SecretFamily:="aws";
    TargetFileName=/\.azure\// | SecretFamily:="azure";
    TargetFileName=/gcloud\// | SecretFamily:="gcp";
    TargetFileName=/\.kube\// | SecretFamily:="k8s";
    TargetFileName=/\.docker\// | SecretFamily:="docker";
    TargetFileName=/\.npmrc/ | SecretFamily:="npm";
    TargetFileName=/\.git-credentials|\.config\/gh\// | SecretFamily:="git";
    TargetFileName=/\.ssh\/id_/ | SecretFamily:="ssh";
    *;
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId], function=[count(field=SecretFamily, distinct=true, as=DistinctFamilies), collect([SecretFamily, TargetFileName])])
| DistinctFamilies>=3

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer

status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

Actions on Objectives
